title: Meet a mouse whose brain cortex is made up of human cells
raw_excerpt: Multiple cameras tracked a mouse as it wandered around a small arena. A computer charted its position and speed, leaving Pong-like traces on a monitor. The reason to watch this rodent so carefully? Nearly half its brain volume had been replaced with human cells. The effort to mix the brain tissues of distant species is being reported today in the journal Nature by a team at Stanford University, led by neuroscientist Sergiu Pașca. Pașca’s group previously showed that human brain “organoids”—small blobs of neural tissue—could survive, and even function, after being injected into the heads of baby rodents . Now, Pașca has taken things a step further by genetically modifying mice so their brains don’t fully develop in the first place. These modified mice are missing most cells of both the cortex and the hippocampus, two key brain areas. That creates much more room for the human cells to take hold, he says. “Human cells that are placed in these animals will divide, will grow, and within a few weeks to a few months they will take most of that space,” he says. Pașca says one surprising discovery is that the mice lacking brain tissue seemed fairly normal—they walked around and squeaked. But they did have memory problems. In a maze test, they couldn’t remember what parts they’d explored. The mice with the added human cells, by contrast, performed better on the maze test. That means the human tissue is playing some role in the animals’ cognition. Pașca believes what he is calling “xen…
summary: 斯坦福大学 Sergiu Pașca 团队在《Nature》报告，将人类脑类器官细胞注入小鼠大脑后，几乎占据其皮层近一半体积，小鼠仍能正常活动、被摄像头追踪行为。这是跨物种脑组织混合迄今最激进的一次尝试，为研究人类神经回路、精神疾病与药物筛选提供了活体平台，同时也把神经伦理争议推到台前。

title: The AI data center e-waste problem is huge — and getting bigger
raw_excerpt: E-waste from the AI boom has been vastly underestimated, a new report warns. By 2050, it could become enough trash to fill 23 million shipping containers - roughly enough 40-foot containers to circle the world six times if lined up in a row. It's a significantly higher estimate of AI's e-waste than previous studies have found because the authors of the new report factor in all the infrastructure needed to support servers in data centers. The broader scope provides a clearer picture of junk AI leaves behind, according to the nonprofit Basel Action Network (BAN) , which published the paper today. summary: 非营利组织 Basel Action Network 发布报告警告，AI 数据中心产生的电子垃圾被严重低估：若把支撑服务器所需的全部基础设施计算在内，到 2050 年废弃物可装满 2300 万个 40 英尺集装箱，足以绕地球六圈。报告把算力扩张的环境代价从「芯片」扩展到供电、冷却、机架等全链条，为 AI 可持续性争论提供了新数据。

title: Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush
raw_excerpt: According to The Information , Apple is planning to get back into the server game and might just pair up with Nvidia to make it happen. But the growing demand for compute power as the AI industry continues to expand has apparently led the company to believe there is an opening for its powerful but efficient ARM-based M processors. summary: 据 The Information 报道，苹果计划重返服务器市场，并可能与 Nvidia 合作，利用其高能效 ARM 架构 M 系列芯片切入 AI 算力供给。苹果 2011 年停产 Xserve 后基本退出企业级硬件，如今 Mac Mini、Mac Studio 已因 AI 开发者抢购而缺货，这一动向意味着苹果可能从「AI 算力消费者」变成供给方，重塑数据中心芯片格局。

title: alibaba/open-code-review
